title: The helmet, the child, and Hector's prayer
intro: A frightened baby briefly interrupts the prospect of death. Hector imagines his son's future, then sends Andromache home.

notes.text: ὀρέγω 3sg aor mid, reached out for, with gen; οὗ possessive gen, his own, agreeing with παιδός.
ἄψ, back; κλίνω 3sg aor pass, leaned / shrank aside. The child recoils into his nurse's bosom.
ἰάχω pres ptc, crying out; ἀτύζομαι aor pass ptc, startled / frightened; ὄψιν acc of what causes fear, his father's appearance.
ταρβέω aor ptc, having taken fright at; acc objects χαλκόν and λόφον.
λόφος, helmet crest; ἱππιοχαίτης, made of horsehair / horse-maned.
κόρυς gen sg κόρυθος; ἀκρότατος superlative of ἄκρος: from the very top of the helmet.
νεύω pres ptc acc masc, nodding, agreeing with λόφον; νοέω aor ptc, noticing. δεινόν adverbial, terribly.
γελάω 3sg aor, laughed; αἱρέω 3sg aor mid, took off. The singular first verb precedes two subjects.
κάρα, head: gen sg. Distinguish κράτος, strength, whose gen is κράτεος / κράτους.
κατατίθημι 3sg aor, set down; παμφανάω pres ptc acc fem, shining brightly, of the helmet.
ὅς possessive, his own; κυνέω 3sg aor, kissed; πάλλω 3sg aor, dandled / tossed in his hands.
ἐπεύχομαι aor mid ptc, praying; δίδωμι 2pl aor imperative, grant. Acc + inf follows: grant that this child become…
ἀριπρεπής acc sg masc, conspicuous / distinguished, with dat Τρώεσσιν, among the Trojans.
βίη acc of respect, strong in might; ἶφι, with might, an old instrumental form; ἀνάσσω pres inf, rule, with gen Ἰλίου.
εἶπον 3sg aor opt of wish, may someone say; ἀμείνων comparative, better, with gen of comparison πατρός.
ἄνειμι pres ptc acc masc, coming back from war; understood object of someone's seeing, as they say the words of 479.
φέρω 3sg pres opt of wish; ἔναρα, stripped armor / spoils, neut pl; βροτόεις, bloodstained, from βρότος, gore.
κτείνω aor ptc nom masc, having killed; δήϊος, hostile / enemy.
χαίρω 3sg aor pass-form opt with active sense, may she rejoice; φρήν acc of respect, in her heart.
ἑός possessive, his own; κηώδης dat sg, fragrant, describing κόλπῳ, the bosom / fold of her robe.
δακρυόεν neut adverbial, tearfully; γελάω aor ptc fem, smiling. A compressed juxtaposition of grief and joy.
πόσις, husband; καταρέζω 3sg aor, stroked / caressed. χειρί dat of means.
ἀκαχίζομαι 2sg pres mid imperative, uncontracted: grieve / distress yourself; μή gives the prohibition.
αἶσα, allotted portion / fate; ὑπέρ + acc, beyond. προϊάπτω 3sg fut, send forth / hurl to Hades.
φεύγω perf mid/pass-form ptc acc masc, with active sense here, escaped; εἰμί inf. Together a perfect infinitival expression after φημι.
μοῖρα is object of escaping; τινά is acc subject of the infinitive, further specified by κακόν / ἐσθλόν: no man, coward or brave.
ἐπήν = ἐπεὶ ἄν; γίγνομαι 3sg aor subj, is born. τὰ πρῶτα adverbial, at the very first.
κομίζω pres imperative, attend to; ἱστός, loom; ἠλακάτη, distaff, the staff holding unspun wool.
ἐποίχομαι pres inf, go about / attend to work; dependent on κέλευε, tell the attendants to…
τοί relative = οἵ; ἐγγίγνομαι 3pl perf active, have been born in, hence are natives of Troy. Epic -άασιν beside -ᾶσιν.
